subject: Inference hosting preference confirmation & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@fintechco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Inference hosting preference confirmation & next steps

Hi Jenna — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have a shared reference and a few clarifying questions before we lock in the POC scope.

High-level notes from discovery:
- Workloads: interactive chat (low latency) + nightly batch embedding jobs
- Latency SLO: ~200ms p95 for chat; embeddings can tolerate higher latency
- Peak throughput: ~20 concurrent chat sessions, batch window ~3 hours/night
- Current architecture: most traffic via OtherAI API; heavy batch runs on in-house GPU cluster (8x A100 equivalent)
- Compliance: SOC 2 required, customer-managed KMS preferred, data residency US-East

Key questions for you:
1) Do you have a firm preference between Hosted API, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), or Private (VPC/on-prem)? You mentioned compliance requirements that might push toward VPC — want to confirm.
2) Any non-negotiable network constraints (no egress to third-party clouds, strict peering rules, IP allowlists)?
3) Migration timeline target (POC → pilot → production)? Any procurement milestones we should align to?

Three pragmatic options to consider (we can detail these in the technical deep-dive):
A) Hosted API trial: fastest path to validate functional parity. Good for short-term evaluation, limited custom networking.
B) Dedicated capacity + VPC peering: reserved GPU pool with private network connection and customer-managed KMS — good balance of performance and compliance.
C) Private deployment (VPC or on-prem): recommended only if procurement requires no third-party control or air-gapped operation — larger upfront work but maximum control.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), migration-checklist.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 45KB).

Proposed next step: technical deep-dive with your infra + security and our serving engineering (30–45m). I have availability Wed 2026-07-15 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue 2026-07-21 09:00–10:00 PT. Which works best for your team?

Thanks — I’ll loop Monica into technical coordination.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Jenna Park <jenna@fintechco.com>

Date: 2026-07-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference hosting preference confirmation & next steps

Karthik — thanks for the summary, this captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity with VPC peering because we need private networking and customer KMS. We would consider Private (VPC/on-prem) only if procurement insists on no third-party-managed control or for specific PCI-scoped flows.
- Migration constraints: our product team wants model parity with the OtherAI setup (same model family, similar tokenization). We run heavy nightly batches on our cluster — want to avoid a big cost spike.
- Security: SOC 2 is required; SSO (SAML) and KMS integration are procurement checkpoints. We will also need audit logs for token-level access.

Action items for us: Marcus (cc’d) will pull the current throughput traces and a sanitized sample dataset. Procurement will flag any contractual must-haves (I expect SAML and KMS to be in the list).

Scheduling: Wed 7/15 10:00 PT looks good for an initial technical review for our infra lead, but Marcus asked if we can also include security (he will confirm).

Thanks — Jenna
Jenna Park
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCo

> Karthik — thanks for the summary, this captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side:
> 
> - Preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity with VPC peering because we need private networking and customer KMS. We would consider Private (VPC/on-prem) only if procurement insists on no third-party-managed control or for specific PCI-scoped flows.

Thanks — helpful context. To make the upcoming technical deep-dive productive, I’m proposing a concrete agenda and a short pre-POC checklist below. I’ve attached a one-page agenda (redwood-technical-deepdive-agenda.docx).

Proposed technical deep-dive agenda (30–45m):
- Quick rollup (5m): goals, SLOs, migration constraints
- Network/security (10m): VPC peering options, KMS flow, SSO/SAML, audit logging
- Performance/cost (10m): perf targets, baseline from your traces, cost tradeoffs across hosted/dedicated/private
- Migration approach (10m): canary with Dedicated pool → workload migration → optional Private handoff
- Action items and next steps (5m)

Pre-POC checklist (what we need from FintechCo to scope the POC):
1) Sample anonymized traces and a representative dataset (Marcus indicated he would provide)
2) A list of required compliance controls (SOC 2 artifacts desired; any PCI-scope notes)
3) Expected timeline / go-live target (why this matters for reserve contract sizing)
4) Primary contact for procurement/security (name + email)

POC proposal (high level):
- Fast path: Spin up Dedicated reserved pool + VPC peering for a 4–6 week POC (validate parity and perf).
- Fallback/next: If procurement requires stricter controls or air-gapped ops, plan a parallel Private deployment assessment (2–3 week discovery).
- Deliverables: perf report, cost delta analysis, migration checklist, and a runbook for production cutover.

Timing: I’ll reserve Wed 2026-07-15 10:00 PT for the deep-dive. Monica (cc) will own the technical invite and pre-call materials.

Let me know if you want to shift to Tue 7/21 instead; otherwise I’ll send a calendar invite and the agenda.

Best,
Karthik
